title: Running the program
heading: Vocabularies
text: Choose a list, then rename its values, say what each means, put them in order, add one, or retire one. Records store a value's key, never its name , so renaming a value rewrites nothing. A new value's key is made from its name and never changes. A value in use is retired, not removed. Records that have it keep it; new records cannot choose it. Some lists can only be renamed. A severity sets a clock, a kind of link says what it joins, an owner kind decides who may edit. Their names, meanings, and order can be changed here; values are added or taken away with a program pack. A value new records start with cannot be retired , such as a system's lifecycle "in service".

title: Running the program
heading: Who may accept what
text: The table on the Program page shows, for each rating, how often a risk is reviewed and who may accept it when it is above appetite: Residual rating Reviewed every May be accepted Low 24 months No acceptance is needed Moderate 12 months For up to 24 months, by a leader of the unit or above High 6 months For up to 12 months, by a leader whose limit reaches high Critical 3 months For up to 6 months, by a leader whose limit reaches critical A leader's limit is set with the role. A sensible start: unit leaders at moderate, division leaders at high, and one or two executives at critical.

title: Running the program
heading: Change the program with a pack
text: The scoring method, cadences, the acceptance table, and the vocabularies (kinds of system, data classes, owner kinds, and so on) are held as one document, a program pack . uv run riskwren program export --output program.json # write the one in force uv run riskwren program import program.json --dry-run # check an edited one uv run riskwren program import program.json # load it An import checks the whole pack first and reports every problem together. A scoring method in which a rating falls as likelihood or impact rises is refused. A changed method becomes a new version: assessments already made keep the version they were made under, and every open risk is read again from what was loaded, as

title: Running the program
heading: Questionnaires
text: A questionnaire is a set of questions RiskWren asks people: to attest that a control still operates, to look again at a risk they own, to confirm that a unit's records are complete. Admin → Questionnaires lists them. Anyone signed in can read one and try it; those who run the program change them. A new installation has four, written for RiskWren: Questionnaire Asks Control attestation A control's owner: does it still operate as described, is there evidence in date, and are you still the right person to answer for it? Risk self-assessment A risk's owner: does it still stand, what has changed, and are its rating and plan still right? Unit completeness check A unit's steward: is everything the

title: Running the program
heading: Questions that appear by condition
text: A question, or a whole section, can be asked only when an earlier answer makes it relevant. "What is different from the statement?" is asked only of someone who said the control operates partly or not at all. So nobody answers what does not apply to them, and what is asked is short. A rule looks only at questions asked before it, so showing and hiding can never run in a circle. An answer to a question that an earlier answer has since hidden is dropped. It cannot go on deciding what else is asked. The form reacts as it is filled in, and the server decides again when the answers are sent. The two use the same rules, held together by one file of test cases.

title: Running the program
heading: Versions
text: Edit changes a questionnaire's sections, questions, their kinds and options, and when each is asked, with the form as it will be asked shown beneath. Saving changed questions publishes a new version . Earlier versions are never altered. An answer is read against the version it was given to. Reword a question or remove one, and what people answered before still reads as it was asked then. A draft begun under one version is finished under that version. A built-in questionnaire you have edited is yours from then on, and a later release leaves it alone. One you have not touched is brought up to date, as a new version. Versions lists every one, with who published it and what they said had changed

title: Running the program
heading: Campaigns
text: A campaign asks a set of people for one thing by a date, and shows who has answered. Compliance → Campaigns → Start a campaign (an assessor or a manager, for the units they cover). Campaign Asks For Control attestation The owners of controls Does each control still operate as described, is its evidence in date, and are you still the right owner? Risk self-assessment The owners of risks Does each risk still stand, what has changed, and are its rating and plan still right? Unit completeness check The stewards of units Is everything the unit has on record, with the right owners? System security profile The owners of systems What each system holds, who can reach it, and who patches, backs up, an

title: Running the program
heading: Following one
text: A campaign's page shows how far it has got, what those who answered said, coverage by unit with the least covered first, and every item with who was asked. Each figure is the count of the list beneath it. Remind tells everyone who still owes something, once, with how many. The scheduled reminders do the same as the date approaches, and tell a unit's steward and then its leader about what stays unanswered. Close ends a campaign and keeps what was answered. Cancel it is for one started in error.

title: Running the program
heading: What an answer sets in motion
text: Answers are kept as given, and some need someone else to act. Those people are told. Answer Who is told A control only partly operates, or does not The unit's assessors, managers, and stewards Someone else should own this control The unit's stewards A risk no longer stands, or its rating is no longer right The unit's stewards, assessors, and managers A unit's records need attention The assessors and managers who cover it An attestation is recorded on the control, with who said it and when. It is never a test : see An attestation is not a test .

title: Running the program
heading: Committee sessions
text: Reports → Committee sessions holds the meetings of the risk and compliance committees. A unit's leaders, or a manager, plan one: its committee, the day it meets, and the unit it answers to. Whoever plans it is its owner, and sees it on Home in the fortnight before it meets. The agenda is drawn from the register: a risk, an issue, an exception, a control, a document, an agreement, a scope, an objective, or an assessment, each with what the committee is asked; or a topic of its own. Items are put in order, and taken off until something is decided about them. A decision is recorded on each item: noted, approved, declined, or deferred, with what was decided. It shows on the record it was about ,

title: Running the program
heading: When someone leaves
text: Disable the account under Admin → People , or with riskwren users disable . The person is signed out and cannot sign in. Everything they did stays in the history under their name. Nothing they answered for is left without an owner: What they alone owned passes at once to the steward of its unit; where the unit and the units above it have no steward, to its leader; failing that to someone who runs the program; and failing that to the administrator who disabled the account. This covers records of every kind, open actions, treatment plans, and what open campaigns were waiting on them for. Whoever it passes to is told , with a count, and has Name who takes what they held on Home until it is done

title: Running the program
heading: Reminders
text: Everything with a date reminds whoever it is waiting on: actions, risk reviews, issues, evidence, acceptances, exceptions, the next test of each control, what a campaign has asked, the next reading of each indicator, document reviews, and agreements. When Who is told 14 days before the date Whoever it is waiting on The day after the date The same people, as overdue. An overdue test also goes to the assessors, because an owner cannot test their own control Still late after 7 days The steward of the unit Still late after 21 days The unit's leader Each of these is said once for a given date. Moving the date starts again. An agreement is told of further ahead: 30 days before the last day to give

title: Running the program
heading: Key controls and the next test
text: What is known about a control holds for twelve months. A control marked key is due to be tested again after six. Each control's page shows the date its next test is due, and its owners are reminded as it approaches. Marking a control key does not change what its last rating counts for; it brings the next test forward.

title: Running the program
heading: Read the dashboards
text: There are two, each for the whole organization or for one unit and everything beneath it. Reports → Compliance shows how ready each scope is against what it is held to and what stands in the way; it is described in The compliance dashboard . Reports → Risk shows where the register stands: Figure Counts Open risks Risks that are not closed Above appetite Open risks whose residual rating exceeds the appetite for their category Need a decision Those above appetite with neither a plan on time nor an acceptance in force Reviews overdue Open risks past their next review date Ratings in doubt Risks flagged because what is known about their controls got worse Actions overdue Open actions past their

title: Running the program
heading: The history
text: Every change to every record is written to an append-only history in the same transaction as the change: who, when, and each value before and after. Each event is hashed together with the one before it, and the database itself refuses updates and deletes on the history. Each record's History tab shows its own events in plain words. Reports → History shows every change in one place, for managers, auditors, and administrators: narrowed to a person, a record, a kind of record, or a span of dates. It opens on changes to records; sign-ins, exports, and settings are one choice away. Reading is recorded where it matters: every download of an evidence file and every export of a list is an event, wit

title: Running the program
heading: Appearance
text: Admin → Appearance makes the product yours, with a live preview: the product's name and your organization's name; a logo for light and for dark mode, and a tab icon; the default palette (Wren, Slate, or Garnet) and an accent color, which is adjusted for dark mode and refused if text on it could not be read; how ratings are colored: an ordinal ramp from light to dark in one hue, which keeps rating apart from the colors of standing, or a signal ramp from green to red. Each person chooses light, dark, or system mode and a palette for themselves, from the appearance button at the top right.

title: Running the program
heading: Back up and recover
text: Back up the data home, and the database as well if you use PostgreSQL. Evidence files are in the data home under files/ , and the database refers to them. uv run riskwren program export keeps a copy of the program you have shaped. If nobody can sign in, riskwren users adds an administrator or resets a password from the server's own command line. Changes made there are recorded in the history as made at the command line.

title: Configuration
heading: Configuration
text: Configuration This guide is for whoever runs the server. It covers riskwren.toml , environment overrides, the data home, PostgreSQL, running behind a reverse proxy, and the guard on demo installations.

title: Configuration
heading: What is configured where
text: RiskWren keeps two kinds of settings apart. Kind Where it lives Examples How the server runs riskwren.toml and the environment Address, port, database, data home The program and the product's look The database, set in the app or by a program pack Risk categories, appetite, the scoring method, cadences, vocabularies, name, logo, colors This guide is about the first. For the second, see Running the program .

title: Configuration
heading: Where the file is found
text: uv run riskwren init writes a commented riskwren.toml in the current directory. Every command looks for the file in this order: The --config FILE option (short form -c ), given before the command. The RISKWREN_CONFIG environment variable. ./riskwren.toml . uv run riskwren --config /etc/riskwren/riskwren.toml doctor Relative paths in the file are resolved against the file's own directory, not the directory you run from. An installation therefore moves as a unit.

title: Configuration
heading: Every section and key
text: The file has five sections. Only the first three matter for a new installation; [sso] and [mail] are optional. A section or key that RiskWren does not know is an error, not something it ignores. Every problem in the file is reported together.

One is enough for SQLite and small teams base_url "" The public address people use to reach RiskWren, such as "https://riskwren.example.org" . Used for the single sign-on redirect address, and for links in messages RiskWren sends. Set it when you use single sign-on session_idle_hours 12 A sign-in ends after this long without activity session_max_days 7 A sign-in ends after this long in any case scheduler true Run scheduled work inside this server. title: Configuration
heading: Environment overrides
text: Any value can be overridden by an environment variable named RISKWREN_<SECTION>_<KEY> , in capitals. The environment wins over the file. Variable Overrides RISKWREN_SERVER_HOST [server] host RISKWREN_SERVER_PORT [server] port RISKWREN_SERVER_WORKERS [server] workers RISKWREN_SERVER_BASE_URL [server] base_url RISKWREN_SERVER_SESSION_IDLE_HOURS [server] session_idle_hours RISKWREN_SERVER_SESSION_MAX_DAYS [server] session_max_days RISKWREN_DATABASE_URL [database] url RISKWREN_DATA_HOME [data] home RISKWREN_SERVER_PORT=8080 uv run riskwren serve RISKWREN_CONFIG is separate: it names the file itself.

title: Configuration
heading: Secrets are refused in the file
text: riskwren.toml is meant to be safe to read, copy, and keep under version control. RiskWren refuses to start if the file holds a secret: a key that looks like a password, secret, token, or key, or a database address with a password in it. Put secrets in the environment instead. For the database, set the password in PGPASSWORD , or put the whole address, password and all, in RISKWREN_DATABASE_URL .

title: Configuration
heading: The data home
text: The data home is created by init . With the default settings it is ./var . Path Holds The SQLite database When no database address is set brand/ Uploaded logos and the tab icon logs/ The server's log, rotated files/ Evidence files, each stored once under the SHA-256 of its content. Nothing here is served directly exports/ Reserved for exports .riskwren-home A marker that says this directory is a data home Back it up as a whole. With PostgreSQL, back up the database as well. Do not edit its contents by hand. It must be writable by the account that runs the server. Request bodies and tokens are never written to the log.

title: Configuration
heading: Single sign-on
text: You do not need this to use RiskWren. A new installation signs in with an email address and a password that RiskWren keeps, and an evaluation or a small team needs nothing else. Single sign-on is something an administrator adds when the organization wants people to use the account they already have, under its own multi-factor authentication and offboarding. When it is on, it sits beside local accounts and does not replace them. The sign-in page shows the organization's button first, with the password form folded beneath it. An administrator can always sign in with a password, so a provider that is down or misconfigured never locks everyone out. RiskWren speaks OpenID Connect: the authorizati

title: Configuration
heading: What you set, and where
text: What Where The provider's issuer and RiskWren's client ID [sso] in riskwren.toml The client secret An environment variable, RISKWREN_SSO_CLIENT_SECRET unless you name another RiskWren's public address [server] base_url , so the redirect address is always the same Which of the provider's roles or groups give which role here In the app: Admin → Single sign-on The redirect address to give the provider is <base_url>/api/v1/sso/callback . Admin → Single sign-on shows it, before and after you set anything up.

heading: With Microsoft Entra ID

Name it, choose Accounts in this organizational directory only , and add a Web redirect URI: your base_url followed by /api/v1/sso/callback . From the registration's Overview , copy the Application (client) ID and the Directory (tenant) ID . Under Certificates & secrets , add a client secret and copy its Value . It is shown once. title: Configuration
heading: With another provider
text: Register RiskWren as a confidential web client with the redirect address above. Set issuer to the address whose /.well-known/openid-configuration the provider serves, and client_id to what it gave you. Have it put a person's groups or roles in a claim, and name that claim in roles_claim (many providers call it groups ). If the provider says email_verified is true for its addresses, leave trust_email as it is.

title: Configuration
heading: Roles from the provider
text: Admin → Single sign-on lists mappings. Each says: everyone the provider gives this value gets this role here. Role here For Works in a unit One unit. Membership grants nothing by itself; it decides what a member sees Steward, Leader One unit, and everything beneath it. A leader's mapping also says what they may accept Assessor, Manager The whole organization, or one unit Auditor, Administrator The whole organization Roles given this way are set again at every sign-in . Take the role away at the provider and it is gone here the next time the person signs in. A shorter session_max_days shortens the wait. Roles given by hand under Admin → People are left alone, and are shown apart from those th

title: Configuration
heading: Who a person is
text: A person is known by the provider's own identifier for them, never by an address alone. The first time someone signs in: if an account here has the address the provider vouches for, the two are joined, and from then on the provider's identifier is what counts; otherwise an account is made for them, with the roles their mappings give, unless create_accounts is false . A disabled account cannot come in through the provider. Signing out of RiskWren does not sign anyone out of the provider.

title: Configuration
heading: Passwords, once it is on
text: With local_sign_in = true , anyone who has a password may still use it. With false , only administrators may. There is no setting that removes the administrator's password, on purpose: it is the way in when the provider cannot be reached.

title: Configuration
heading: Try it on a laptop
text: scripts/dev_identity_provider.py is a stand-in provider for trying this out. It has a fixed list of people and no passwords, and its signing key is published in the file, so it proves nothing and listens only on the machine it runs on. uv run python scripts/dev_identity_provider.py Then set issuer = "http://127.0.0.1:8099" , client_id = "riskwren-dev" , and trust_email = true under [sso] , and start RiskWren with RISKWREN_SSO_CLIENT_SECRET=dev-secret in its environment.

title: Configuration
heading: Use PostgreSQL
text: SQLite is the default and needs no setup. Use PostgreSQL when many people will use RiskWren at once or you want more than one server process. The features and the data model are the same on both, and the test suite runs on both. Install the driver, which is optional: `` bash uv sync --extra postgres `` Create an empty database and a role that owns it, with your usual PostgreSQL tools. title: Configuration
heading: Run behind a reverse proxy
text: RiskWren speaks plain HTTP and expects a reverse proxy to terminate TLS in front of it. Keep host = "127.0.0.1" when the proxy is on the same machine. Have the proxy send X-Forwarded-Proto: https . RiskWren marks its session cookie Secure when the request arrived over HTTPS, by that header or directly. Forward the Host header unchanged. title: Configuration
heading: The demo and the network
text: A demo organization signs in anyone who asks as any of its sample people, with no password. So a demo's server listens only on the machine it runs on: serve refuses any other host, and the sample sign-in refuses requests from other machines. If you do want to show a demo to others on a network you trust: uv run riskwren --config demo/riskwren.toml serve --host 0.0.0.0 --demo-on-network Anyone who can reach it can then sign in as the demo's risk manager or administrator. Never do this with a database that holds anything real; a demo database holds nothing that is.

title: The API
heading: The API
text: API Everything the web app does, it does through a JSON API under /api/v1 . This guide covers how to sign in, how answers and errors are shaped, how lists page, and what routes there are. The exact shape of every request and answer is in the OpenAPI document: openapi.json in this directory, or /api/openapi.json on a running server. This release has no API tokens. A program signs in as an account, with that account's password, and holds a session as a browser does. Tokens scoped to a role arrive with integrations in a later release; see the roadmap . Until 1.0, routes may change between releases. Changes are listed in the changelog .

title: The API
heading: Sign in
text: curl -s -c cookies.txt -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"email": "you@example.org", "password": "…"}' \ http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/session The answer describes who you are, and sets a session cookie, riskwren_session : { "data": { "account": {"id": 12, "name": "Your Name", "email": "you@example.org"}, "roles": ["manager"], "permissions": {"…": true}, "units": {"manager": null}, "member_units": [4], "has_password": true, "csrf_token": "…" }, "meta": {} } In units , each scoped role lists the units it covers, or null for the whole organization. GET /api/v1/session returns the same for the session you hold, or 401 if you hold none. DELETE /api/v1/session signs out.

title: The API
heading: Changing things
text: Every request that changes anything ( POST , PUT , PATCH , DELETE ) must carry the session's CSRF token in a header: curl -s -b cookies.txt -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'X-CSRF-Token: …' \ -d '{"name": "Freezer farm", "kind": "device", "criticality": "critical", "org_unit_id": 4}' \ http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/systems Without it the answer is 403. If the request carries an Origin header, it must match the host, or the request is refused.

title: The API
heading: Editing a record someone else is editing
text: Records carry a version . Send the version you read with a PATCH , and if someone else has changed the record since, the answer is 409 and nothing is saved. Read it again and decide what to do.

title: The API
heading: Answers
text: Every successful answer has the same envelope: {"data": …, "meta": {…}} data is one object or a list. meta carries what is about the answer and not in it: paging for a list, or a count of what else changed. Times are UTC in ISO 8601. Dates with no time, such as a due date, are YYYY-MM-DD .

A rating is a judgment."} ], "instance": "/api/v1/risks/RSK-0002/assessments" } Status Meaning 400 The request could not be carried out as asked 401 Nobody is signed in, or the email address and password do not match 403 You are signed in but may not do this, or the CSRF token is missing. detail says which 404 No such thing, or none that you may see. title: The API
heading: What the API will not do
text: It never returns a record you may not see, and never counts one. It never edits an assessment, a control rating, a test result, or an acceptance. Each is superseded by a new one. A file can say what a risk or a control is, and not how it has been judged. It never changes the history. There is no route that does.

title: Command reference
heading: Command reference
text: Command reference Every riskwren command. This page is written from the program itself, so it always matches the version it ships with. Run commands with uv run riskwren … from the project directory. Options that come before the command apply to all of them: riskwren [-h] [--version] [-c FILE] [-v | -q] COMMAND ...

title: Command reference
heading: Commands
text: Command What it does riskwren init Set up a new installation riskwren serve Run the web server riskwren demo Build a fictional organization to explore riskwren db Look after the database schema riskwren users Manage accounts from the command line riskwren verify Check that the history has not been altered riskwren frameworks See and load what the organization is held to riskwren program Move the program between installations riskwren doctor Check that this installation is healthy riskwren jobs See scheduled work, or run it now riskwren mail Send waiting email, or test the mail settings

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren init
text: Write a configuration file if there is none, create the data home, create or upgrade the database, and create the first administrator if there is none. Safe to run again. Option Meaning --force overwrite an existing configuration file --admin-email EMAIL create the first administrator with this address --admin-name NAME the first administrator's name --password-stdin read the password from standard input instead of asking

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren serve
text: Run RiskWren's web server. It refuses to start on a database whose schema is behind; run riskwren db upgrade first. Option Meaning --host address to listen on (default: from the configuration) --port PORT port to listen on (default: from the configuration) --workers WORKERS server processes (default: from the configuration) --reload restart when the code changes (development) --demo-on-network let a demo organization listen beyond this machine (anyone who reaches it can sign in as its sample people)

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren demo
text: Build the Northmere Institute for Health Research, a fictional organization with two years of history, in its own directory. Everything in it is made by the same code the app uses. Start it with the command it prints. Option Meaning PATH where to build it (default: ./demo) --seed SEED a different number gives a different Northmere --port PORT the port its server will use (default: 8020) --force rebuild a demo that is already there

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren db
text: Look after the database schema.

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren db upgrade
text: Apply any migrations the database has not had. Export first: an upgrade cannot be undone except by restoring.

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren db current
text: Show which migration the database is at, and which this version expects. Exits with 1 when they differ.

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren users
text: Manage accounts from the command line: for setting up, and for getting back in when nobody can sign in. Everyday account management is in the app, under Admin. Changes made here are recorded in the history as made at the command line.

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren users add
text: Add an account. It asks for a password unless --password-stdin or --invite is given. Option Meaning EMAIL the email address the person signs in with --name the person's name --title their job title --role ROLE a role: admin, manager, assessor, auditor, steward=unit:CODE, or leader=unit:CODE,limit:RATING; manager and assessor may also take unit:CODE (may be repeated) --unit CODE a unit they work in, by code (may be repeated) --password-stdin read the password from standard input instead of asking --invite add them without a password: they can be named on records now, and sign in once they are given a password or use single sign-on

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren users list
text: List every account with its status and roles.

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren users disable
text: Stop an account signing in and end its sessions. Its history is kept, and what the person alone answered for passes to the steward of its unit until someone is named for good. The last active administrator cannot be disabled. Option Meaning EMAIL the account's email address

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren users enable
text: Let a disabled account sign in again. Option Meaning EMAIL the account's email address

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren users reset-password
text: Give an account a new password and end its sessions. Option Meaning EMAIL the account's email address --password-stdin read the password from standard input instead of asking

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren users roles
text: Show an account's roles, or with --set replace the roles granted in RiskWren. Roles mapped from an identity provider are left alone. The last active administrator cannot lose that role. Option Meaning EMAIL the account's email address --set ROLE a role: admin, manager, assessor, auditor, steward=unit:CODE, or leader=unit:CODE,limit:RATING; manager and assessor may also take unit:CODE (may be repeated); with none, removes every role

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren verify
text: Recompute the hash chain over every event in the history and report the first one that does not hold, then check every published version of a document against the fingerprint the history took when it was published. Exits with 1 if either does not hold.

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren frameworks
text: A framework is a source of requirements: a public standard, a regulation, an agreement's terms. Four public ones ship with RiskWren and are loaded at installation. Others are loaded from a pack file, or entered in the app.

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren frameworks list
text: List every framework.

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren frameworks load
text: Load a framework from a pack file, or the built-in ones that are missing. A pack is checked whole first and refused whole if anything is wrong. Option Meaning FILE the pack to load --builtin load the built-in frameworks not yet here, and the publishers' mappings for those that are --dry-run check the pack, and load nothing

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren frameworks show
text: Show a framework's publisher, version, license, and source. Option Meaning KEY the framework's key, such as nist-csf

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren program
text: The program is everything a risk and compliance team configures: vocabularies, the risk categories and their appetite, the scoring method, cadences, and who may accept what. It lives in the database and moves as one file.

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren program export
text: Write the whole program as one JSON document, to a file or to standard output. Option Meaning --output , -o FILE write to this file

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren program import
text: Load a program pack. The whole pack is checked first, and nothing is loaded unless all of it can be. A new scoring method is published as a new version; assessments already made keep the version they were made under, and every open risk is read again from what was loaded: its ratings, its standing, and its next review. Option Meaning FILE the pack to load --dry-run say what would change, and change nothing

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren doctor
text: Check the configuration, the data home, the database and its schema, and the history. Exits with 1 if anything must be fixed.

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren jobs
text: Scheduled work brings risks up to date with the calendar, sends reminders, and sends email where that is set up. The server does this by itself while it runs. These commands are for seeing how it is going, and for running it from a scheduled task where the server's own scheduler is turned off.

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren jobs run
text: Run every job that is due. With a job's name, run that one now whether or not it is due. A job another process is running is left to it. Option Meaning JOB one job to run now

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren mail
text: Email is optional. Where it is set up, the server sends it by itself while it runs. These commands are for testing the settings and for sending by hand.

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren mail run
text: Queue notices and daily summaries, and send what is waiting. Exits with 1 if a message could not be sent.

title: Command reference
heading: riskwren mail test
text: Send one message now to the account with this address, and say whether the mail server accepted it. Option Meaning EMAIL the account to send it to

heading: Changelog
text: Changelog RiskWren follows semantic versioning. Each wave of the roadmap is a release. Before 1.0, a release may contain breaking changes; they are listed under Breaking .

title: Changelog
text: Wave 4, Policy and obligations : the organization's own word, and what it has promised others. Policies, standards, procedures, and guidelines are written or linked here, approved by named people, published as versions that never change, reviewed on a cadence, read in a library on any device, and acknowledged by the people they apply to. Each is tied to the controls it directs and the requirements it answers. Agreements carry their dates and the terms they impose on the scopes that hold what they cover. A framework's new version is loaded beside the old, and a scope moves to it when its keepers say so. Strategic objectives and committee sessions connect the register to the organization's aim

title: Changelog
heading: Known limits
text: Single sign-on has been tested against the stand-in provider in scripts/dev_identity_provider.py , which speaks the same protocol, and not yet against a live Microsoft Entra ID tenant. Email has been tested against a test server, not through an organization's mail service. Two records that are the same thing can be found, and not yet merged. The questionnaire editor writes a condition with one part. A condition with several parts is written in the questionnaire's document. Who may accept what, the number of levels and ratings, and how much a control may reduce a rating are changed with a program pack, not in the app.

title: Changelog
text: Wave 2, Compliance : test once, satisfy many. Load a framework, see it mapped to the organization's controls, define the scope that must meet it, test each control once, hold the evidence, and follow what fails through an issue to a closure someone else confirms. heading: Upgrading from 0.1.0
text: Run uv sync , then uv run riskwren db upgrade (migrations 0007 to 0013). Every row is kept. The upgrade loads the four public frameworks and the mappings the common controls carry to them. It does not map the controls you already have: each one that came from the library offers its mappings on its Requirements tab.

title: Changelog
heading: Added
text: Frameworks. Four public frameworks load at installation, each built from its publisher's own machine-readable file and carried as published: the NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0, NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 (release 5.2.0) with the Low, Moderate, High, and Privacy baselines, NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 3, and the HIPAA Security Rule. Each shows its publisher, version, license, and source. Anyone signed in can browse a framework's tree, search it, narrow it to a baseline, and read any requirement in full (migration 0007).
